exposure: luteal phase short-acting GnRH-a long protocol (LPS)
cohort: A total of 4510 neonates born from 3530 assisted reproductive technology (ART) cycles using either early-follicular long-acting GnRH-a long protocol (EFL) or luteal phase short-acting GnRH-a long protocol (LPS) at a single center between January 1, 2014, and June 30, 2017.
finding: The early-follicular long-acting GnRH-a (EFL) and luteal phase short-acting GnRH-a (LPS) protocols demonstrated similar rates of congenital anomalies, birth weight, and gestational age at delivery, indicating comparable offspring safety, though multiple pregnancies were identified as an independent risk factor for congenital abnormalities.
